sections.heading: Myocardial oxygen supply and demand
sections.html:
The left ventricle extracts about 70–75% of the oxygen delivered to it even at rest, so a rise in demand is met almost entirely by a rise in coronary blood flow, not by more extraction.

[[figure:smp-fig01]]

Flow to the left ventricle occurs mostly in diastole, when the contracting wall no longer compresses intramural vessels. Tachycardia shortens diastole and so limits supply just as demand rises.
